 JUDGMENT
The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident dated 11.06.2020.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, On 11.06.2020 at about 6.35pm when the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-V-4824 on Chikkanayakanahalli Gattahalli Main Road slowly and cautiously, infront of Anjaneya Temple, Chikkanayakanahalli, a Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MM-2986 came from opposite direction at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life, without observing traffic rules and regulations, came to his extreme right side i.e., on wrong side of the road and dashed against his motorcycle and caused the accident.
Due to impact the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries.

3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, immediately after the accident he was taken to St.John's Hospital, wherein admitted and treated with surgery and discharged with the advise for regular follow up treatment.
So far he has spent huge amount towards hospitalization and medicines.
Prior to the date of accident he was hale and healthy, doing Plumbing work with one Anwar Sharief and SCCH - 25 4 MVC No. 4449/2020 earning a sum of Rs.18,000/- per month.
Due to the accident he could not work and he could not do his day today activities also and lost all his income.
The accident is due to the sole negligence of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MM- 2986.
The HSR Layout police have registered a case against the driver of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.48/2020 p/u/Sec.279 & 338 of IPC.
Therefore, the 1 st respondent being the RC owner and the 3rd respondent being the insurer of the said offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to him.
Hence, this petition.
During the pendency of the case, the Respondent No.2 deleted as per Order dated 09.09.2022.

On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:-
1.
Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing reg.No.KA-51-MM-5986 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?
6. The Petitioner in order to prove his case has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.11.
Mr. Mohan C. - Medical Record Officer at St. John's Hospital got examined as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.12 to P.14.
Dr.Avinash Parthasarathy got examined as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.15 to 17.
On the other side, the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.
Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.

8. On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3: As per the final order,
 for the following:-
 REASONS  9. Issue No.1:-

In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MM-2986, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.6.
He has reiterated the contents of the petition in his affidavit filed in lieu of his chief examination.
During his cross examination by the counsel for R-3, he has stated that on the date of accident, he was going from Chikkanayakanahalli to Ghattahalli.
He does not know if the accident spot was NH but it was a service road and there was two way traffic.
Further admitted that it SCCH - 25 7 MVC No. 4449/2020 was head on collision.

He did not see the car, it came suddenly Hari Malik vs Manjunatha S.P on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184703316/
3 and hit him.

sentences.text: In order to prove their defence, the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents.
10. As per FIR, it was registered on the next day of the accident on the complaint of the petitioner's friend Mr.Amar Kumar at Ex.P.1.
Ex.P.2 spot sketch shows that the accident caused due to head on collision between Car and motorcycle.
Ex.P.3 spot mahazar conducted on 12.06.2020 from 11.00am to 12.00pm.

Ex.P.4 IMV report shows that the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-51-MM-2986 got damaged to its (1) Front right side bumper, (2) Front right side head light and indicator, (3) Front right side fender damaged.
The petitioner's motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-V-4824 also got damaged to its (1) Front wheel mud guard, (2) Crash guard, (3) scratch mark found on head light mask damaged.
Ex.P.5 wound Certificate it is mentioned that Hari Malik got injuries in an RTA on 11.06.2020 on 7.00pm at Chikkanayakanahalli.
The police have conducted investigation and filed the charge sheet SCCH - 25 8 MVC No. 4449/2020 as per Ex.P.6 against the driver of the Car.
All these documents show that there was negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MM-2986.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:-
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.5.
As per Ex.P.5 the Petitioner has suffered (1) Crush injury over interior aspect of right ankle extending to dorsum of foot exposing cut tenderness with active building.
(2) Multiple abrasion of various sizes over right leg and foot.
Out of these injuries, Injury No.1 is grievous and injury No.2 is simple in nature.

12. The petitioner has also got examined Mr. Mohan C - Medical Record Officer at st. John's Hospital, Bangalore as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.12 to 14 authorization letter, OP file, Inpatient case sheet.
There is no cross examination of PW.2.
The petitioner has also got examined Dr.Avinash Parthasarathy as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.15 to 17 Recent examination, X-ray and disability assessment proforma.
He has deposed the details of injuries and surgery undergone by the petitioner and diagnosed to have right foot post traumatic crush avulsion injury with tibio-talus dislocation.
He has further stated that the petitioner is suffering permanent physical impairment at 44% and to the whole body disability at 15%.
14. PW.3 in his cross examination has stated that he has not treated the petitioner.
Further admitted that the petitioner has not suffered any fracture.
He has not given grade to the crush injury and the crush injury can not be graded.
Dislocation is reduced as good as normal.
Further admitted that the ROM is only at ankle joint.
The dislocation of the petitioner is reduced and not given cogent reason for ROM.
Further admitted that he has not assessed the functional disability.
SCCH - 25 10 MVC No. 4449/2020 Hari Malik vs Manjunatha S.P on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184703316/

4  Disability:
15.
From the evidence of PW.3 and the documents on record, it is clear that the petitioner has suffered right foot post traumatic crush avulsion injury with tibio-talus dislocation.
So it will be difficult for him to do the work.
He has stated that he was doing Plumbing Work.
This means that he has to sit and stand to do the said work.
This kind of disability will affect his day to day work.
Therefore, considering his age and disability, this court deems it fit to fix the whole body disability at 15%.

Monthly income:
16.
The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was doing Plumbing work and earning Rs.18,000/- per month.
In this regard he has not examined any witness nor produced any documents like Bank statement etc., to prove his earnings.
The accident occurred in the year 2020.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.14,500/- per month.
At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged SCCH - 25 11 MVC No. 4449/2020 about 20 years as could be made out from Ex.P.14/Aadhar Card.
He was hale and healthy before the accident.

Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:-
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:-

After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at St. John's Hospital wherein he was admitted and treated as an inpatient from 11.06.2020 to 22.06.2020 was diagnosed and underwent surgery which can be made out from Ex.P.14/Inpatient case sheet of the said hospital.
Considering that the nature of injuries he has undergone are grievous and simple, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.70,000/- under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines, conveyance, food and nourishment and other incidental expenses etc.
In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.8 for a sum of Rs.85,937/- There is no contrary evidence against these SCCH - 25 12 MVC No. 4449/2020 bills from the Respondents.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the above said amount under this head.

iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:-
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous and simple injuries.
As per the inpatient case sheet it can be found out the duration of treatment of the petitioner in the said hospital.

Therefore, considering the nature of injuries it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least One month time for recovering from the Hari Malik vs Manjunatha S.P on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184703316/
5 injuries sustained by him.

sentences.text: Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.14,500/- under this head.

iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:-
On perusal of Ex.P.7/Notarized copy of Aadhar Card, the birth year of the petitioner is mentioned as 2000.
the accident occurred on 11.06.2020.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is 20 years.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 18.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled SCCH - 25 13 MVC No. 4449/2020 for a sum of Rs.4,69,800/-
(Rs.14,500/- x 12 x 18 x 15%= Rs.4,69,800/-) under this head.
 (v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:-
The Petitioner was aged about 20 years at the time of accident.
He has sustained grievous and simple injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 15% functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.

Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered,
a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.
(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospital, admitted as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioner SCCH - 25 14 MVC No. 4449/2020 is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

17. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.70,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs.85,937/-
3. Loss of income during laid up Rs.14,500/- period 4. Loss of future income Rs.4,69,800/-

5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/- happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/-
nourishment charges TOTAL Rs.6,80,237/-

The Respondent No.3 did not prove its defence.
Therefore, the Respondents being the RC owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

However, as the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent No.3/insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.1/insured SCCH - 25 15 MVC No. 4449/2020 and has to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.15,00,000/- but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.6,80,300/- with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, Issue No.3 is held in the affirmative.
19. Issue No.4:-

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,80,300/- (Rupees Six Lakhs Eighty Thousand and Three Hundred only) along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondent Nos.1 & 3 are jointly and severally SCCH - 25 16 MVC No. 4449/2020 liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.3/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of e-payment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw decree accordingly.
